item.title: Launchy 2026.8
item.description:
A feature release bringing Liquid Glass to macOS 26+, a configurable idle page-revert, smoother live search, and a handful of drag-and-drop and dismiss-gesture fixes. Launchy is now also licensed under AGPL-3.0.

Features

  • NEWAdopted Liquid Glass on macOS 26+ for settings, floaty launcher, search bar, and onboarding, with material fallbacks for older systems
  • NEWAdded configurable idle page-revert setting
  • NEWSoftened accent-color vibrancy and polished the traffic lights
  • NEWFolders now close on background tap instead of hiding the launcher
  • NEWLaunchy now remembers the current page and folder across quick toggles
  • NEWSelf-built copies are now detected via code-signature check, with a hint linking to the official release

Performance

  • PERFPrewarmed search-result icons and cached low-res thumbnails to disk for smoother live search

Fixes

  • FIXFixed grid and folder icon drag-and-drop on macOS 27
  • FIXFixed grid, folder, and search bar clicks being swallowed by the click-outside-to-dismiss gesture
  • FIXRestored background tap-to-dismiss
  • FIXFixed the launcher not appearing when Launchy is selected in the app switcher, not just on Dock icon click (#11)
  • FIXFixed intentionally empty folders being dropped when restoring the arrangement (#16)
  • FIXHardened global hotkey registration for future macOS releases with an event-monitor fallback and failure logging
  • FIXDocumented the icon-catalog build target mismatch

Localization

  • IMPROVEAdded missing translations for system-tool tile strings and the donation callout in all languages
  • IMPROVEAdded missing PrivateBuildLabel and GetOfficialVersionLabel translations

Licensing & Documentation

  • IMPROVERelicensed the project from MIT to AGPL-3.0
  • IMPROVEAdded public build scripts plus CONTRIBUTING and AI_POLICY docs
  • IMPROVERewrote the wiki as a use-case-driven user guide and added a wiki publish script
  • IMPROVESwitched docs and wiki to a consistent first-person voice

Launchy is the free open-source Launchpad alternative macOS users have been waiting for. Fullscreen mode mirrors the classic Launchpad experience but adds richer controls, while Floaty Mode doubles as a HUD with fast toggles that match the new macOS design without changing the behavior you rely on. It scans your apps, caches icons, and keeps a responsive grid ready on every Space - a universal binary that runs natively on both Apple Silicon (M-series) and Intel Macs, all completely free.
